task: I’m trying to narrow down a few law schools in the Maryland/DC area and want a practical outreach plan before I start contacting anyone. On the University of Maryland Carey Law site, please find the actual way I can request admissions materials and also look for at least one upcoming online admissions event with its date and time, because I want to see how easy they make it to get information and whether there’s a virtual event I could realistically attend; open the event details page in its own tab and leave it there so I can look at it later. Then go to the University of Baltimore School of Law site and find the instructions for scheduling an admissions meeting by opening the relevant admissions event or meeting page and pulling the registration link or contact method from the actual details page, and keep that page open too so I can compare the two schools side by side. After that, on American University Washington College of Law’s site, find the PIPS Scholarship page and give me a short plain-English summary of what the scholarship is for, along with the application form link, because funding could change which school I prioritize; if there’s a dedicated scholarship page, leave that open in another tab as proof. Once you’ve gathered all of that, recommend which of these three schools I should contact first based on the best mix of easy admissions outreach and potential funding, and include the specific action or contact details you found for each school so I have a simple next move.
agent_final_answer:
### Law School Admissions & Outreach Plan (MD / DC Area)

---

### 1. University of Maryland Francis King Carey School of Law
* **How to Request Admissions Materials:**
  * **Online Inquiry Form:** Prospective JD applicants can submit the official JD Prospect Inquiry Form at:  
    `https://forms.lsac-unite.org/5814/2027ProspectiveApplicantInquiryForm.html`
  * **Direct Contact:** You can also contact the Office of Admissions directly by email at `admissions@law.umaryland.edu` or by phone at `(410) 706-3492` (Office hours: Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM).
* **Upcoming Online Admissions Event:**
  * **Event:** *Mock Application Review & AMA*
  * **Date & Time:** **Thursday, September 24, 2026, from 5:00 PM to 6:00 PM EDT**
  * *(Upcoming subsequent sessions include: "Interviewing Do's and Don’ts" on Wednesday, September 30, 2026, 5:00 PM–6:00 PM EDT, and "JD Info Session & Application Overview" on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, 12:00 PM–1:00 PM EDT).*
* **Open Tab:**
  * **Tab ID 2136412448:** *2027 Prospects | Webinar Mock App Review 9.24.26*  
    URL: `https://forms.lsac-unite.org/5814/ProspectsWebinar92426.html`

---

### 2. University of Baltimore School of Law
* **Instructions for Scheduling an Admissions Meeting:**
  * **1-on-1 Appointments:** UBalt Law offers scheduled 30-minute individual phone or Zoom appointments with an admissions counselor for advice, profile evaluation, and questions not covered on the website.
  * **Meeting Registration Link:** Submit your details and pick an available 30-minute timeslot (sessions run Wednesdays and Thursdays at 11:00 AM–11:30 AM and 11:30 AM–12:00 PM ET) via the registration form:  
    `https://forms.lsac-unite.org/5810/UBaltLawPhoneCallFall2026.html`
  * **Direct Contact Method:** Email `lawadmissions@ubalt.edu` or call `(410) 837-4459` during office hours (Monday–Friday, 8:30 AM – 4:30 PM).
  * **Virtual Group Option:** They also offer a *Fall Virtual Open House* on **Tuesday, October 27, 2026, 6:00 PM – 7:00 PM ET** via Zoom (`https://ubalt.zoom.us/j/94507089329`, Passcode: `UBaltLaw`, no registration required).
* **Open Tabs:**
  * **Tab ID 2136412449:** *Speak with UBalt Law | Fall 2026* (Phone Call Registration Form)  
    URL: `https://forms.lsac-unite.org/5810/UBaltLawPhoneCallFall2026.html`
  * **Tab ID 2136412301:** *Visit the School of Law* (UBalt Visits, Tours & Events main portal)  
    URL: `https://www.ubalt.edu/law/admission-and-aid/visit/index.cfm`

---

### 3. American University Washington College of Law (AU WCL)
* **Dedicated PIPS Scholarship Page:**
  * URL: `https://www.american.edu/wcl/impact/initiatives-programs/publicinterest/pipsscholarship/index.cfm`
* **Plain-English Summary:**
  * The **Public Interest / Public Service (PIPS) Scholarship** is a full-tuition, 3-year scholarship awarded to incoming (1L) full-time JD students. It is designed for students with strong academic credentials and a demonstrated commitment to public interest or government service who intend to pursue a full-time career in public service upon graduation. In addition to covering full tuition, scholars receive programmatic mentoring, faculty advising, and entry into an active public interest alumni and student community.
* **Application Form Link & Deadlines:**
  * **Application Form Link:** `https://american.co1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6FMJcuOCtqeRJiu`
  * **Requirements & Deadline:** Must submit both the general AU WCL JD application and the separate online PIPS application (which includes three short essays, a resume, and an optional recommendation letter) by **January 31, 2027 at 11:59 PM EST** (applicants are strongly advised to take the LSAT by November).
* **Open Tab:**
  * **Tab ID 2136412452:** *Public Interest/Public Service (PIPS) Scholarship | American University, Washington, DC*  
    URL: `https://www.american.edu/wcl/impact/initiatives-programs/publicinterest/pipsscholarship/index.cfm`

---

### Recommendation: Which School to Contact First

**Top Recommendation:** Contact **American University Washington College of Law (AU WCL)** first if institutional funding is a major decision driver, but start immediate admissions outreach with **University of Baltimore**.

1. **Why AU WCL for Funding Strategy:**  
   The PIPS Scholarship at AU WCL offers complete **full-tuition coverage for all three years**, but it has an early competitive deadline (**January 31, 2027**) with an explicit recommendation to test by November. Because this requires tailored essays and an early application file, reaching out to AU WCL's admissions and financial aid offices now will ensure your application strategy aligns with the PIPS timeline.
2. **Why UBalt for Admissions Outreach:**  
   UBalt makes personal outreach the easiest and fastest of the three: you can directly self-schedule a dedicated **1-on-1 30-minute consultation** on their live calendar starting right away.
3. **Why UMD Carey for Programmatic Overview:**  
   UMD Carey Law is ideal for low-pressure structured learning via their interactive webinar series starting **September 24, 2026**, giving you a direct line to ask admissions questions in real time.

---

### Simple Next Moves & Direct Contact Details

* **American University Washington College of Law:**
  * **Next Action:** Open the Qualtrics form (`https://american.co1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6FMJcuOCtqeRJiu`) to review the 3 essay prompts, and email Admissions (`wcladmit@wcl.american.edu` / 202-274-4101) or Financial Aid (`finaid@wcl.american.edu` / 202-274-4040) to inquire about the PIPS selection timeline.
* **University of Baltimore School of Law:**
  * **Next Action:** Go to Tab `2136412449` (`https://forms.lsac-unite.org/5810/UBaltLawPhoneCallFall2026.html`) and select an upcoming Wednesday/Thursday 30-minute slot for a 1-on-1 call with an admissions counselor, or email `lawadmissions@ubalt.edu` / call `(410) 837-4459`.
* **University of Maryland Carey Law:**
  * **Next Action:** Go to Tab `2136412448` (`https://forms.lsac-unite.org/5814/ProspectsWebinar92426.html`) to register for the September 24 "Mock Application Review & AMA" webinar, and complete the JD inquiry form (`https://forms.lsac-unite.org/5814/2027ProspectiveApplicantInquiryForm.html`).

---

| **2136412301** | *Visit the School of Law* (UBalt Visits & Events) | `https://www.ubalt.edu/law/admission-and-aid/visit/index.cfm` |
| **2136412452** | *Public Interest/Public Service (PIPS) Scholarship \| American University* | `https://www.american.edu/wcl/impact/initiatives-programs/publicinterest/pipsscholarship/index.cfm` |

Institutional Scholarships
Merit Scholarships

The AUWCL Office of Admissions considers all applicants for merit scholarships at the time of their admission; a separate application is not required. Merit scholarship awards primarily consider applicant academic indicators (LSAT/GRE and undergraduate GPA). Merit scholarships for full-time JD students are renewable for up to three academic years per the AUWCL Merit Scholarship Policy. The Office of Admissions generally begins awarding merit scholarship in February and continues throughout the admissions process.

Public Interest Public Service Scholarship

The Public Interest Public Service (PIPS) Scholarship is a full-tuition scholarship awarded to incoming (1L) full-time JD students only. The scholarship is awarded to those with a demonstrated commitment to public service, strong academic credentials, and a desire to pursue a public interest or public service career upon graduation. A separate scholarship application is required.

For more information on the PIPS Scholarship, including the link for the scholarship application, please click here.

Myers Law Scholarship

The Myers Law Scholarship is AUWCL’s most prestigious award and provides one-year scholarships to matriculated full-time JD students (one or two annually; priority given to upper-level students with an AUWCL need-based grant) who show academic promise and demonstrate financial need. Scholarships are funded up to 125 percent of tuition. 

For more information about the Myers Law Scholarship, please visit the Donor-Funded Restricted Scholarships page here.

Donor-Funded Restricted Scholarships

Through the generosity of AUWCL friends and alumni, dozens of named scholarships are awarded annually ranging in amounts from $1,000 to upwards of $20,000 depending on funding levels in a given year. Selection criteria for these scholarships vary. Most commonly awards are based on financial need and academic achievement.

The Restricted Scholarships require a separate application; procedures and selection criteria are announced during the fall semester with the application deadline typically 2-3 weeks after the first announcement.

For more information about Donor-Funded Restricted Scholarships, please click here.

United Methodist Scholarship

The United Methodist Scholarship is awarded each academic year to full-time JD law students who are full members of the United Methodist Church for at least one year prior to application. International students from one of the United Methodist Church Central Conferences must be a member of The United Methodist Church for a minimum of three years. International students from an autonomous Methodist Church (or non-UMC Central Conference) must have been a member of The United Methodist Church within the U.S. for at least three years.

The annual application, along with the required supplemental documentation, must be submitted to the AUWCL Office of Financial Aid by the March deadline listed on the application. The Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) is also required for U.S. citizens and permanent residents. The application is posted annually to the Financial Aid Forms webpage when available.

AUWCL Business Law Scholarship

The AUWCL Business Law Scholarship provides financial support for incoming, full-time JD law students focused on practicing business law and committed to ethically making a positive impact. The application is posted annually to the Office of Financial Aid Prospective Students
